svg.text: With a federated credential: the server acts for the user (OBO)
No federated credential: nothing in the server acts as the user
FIC = federated identity credential on the API app. It trusts the UAMI's token (issuer: the tenant's
v2.0 endpoint, subject: the UAMI's principal, audience api://AzureADTokenExchange), so the
server proves itself for OBO with no client secret. Names: id-abw-mcp-<server>-<region>-001.
Identity and entitlements: who can reach what
Personas, groups and app roles, the five MCP API apps, data RBAC and the server identities
Agents Behind the Wall - diagram 06 of 13 - generated by docs/diagrams/build_diagrams.py
Five personas (abw.<persona>@<tenant-domain>): app roles sit on the user, groups carry the data access
Walls 1 and 2: the app roles in the token decide which tools a person may call
Tools. research: search_research, get_research_note. wall: list_my_wall_crossings, search_deal_documents, get_deal_document. actions: check_restricted_list and list_my_orders (Trade.Read or
Trade.Execute), place_order (Trade.Execute and the Tools.Execute scope; the governed agent also asks a human to approve). private: get_firm_positions, get_credit_limit. vendor: get_market_quote,
get_headlines. The private server is not behind the gateway, so it is Wall 2 that refuses.
Wall 3: group membership decides what the user's own token can read

Cells follow the app roles and tool rules in the code and the group RBAC in the platform template. Priya, Ian and the operator were run live; Wes, Tara and Carla are designed behaviour until each has signed in

once. The Search role covers the whole index: the public/wall split inside it is a server-side filter in the MCP server (Wall 2). sg-abw-demo-all holds Foundry Agent Consumer on the project, so every persona can
talk to the agents. The operator holds no data-plane role: Owner is not data access.
Server identities: the five API apps and the six managed identities

- App roles on the user open the gateway and the MCP server (Walls 1 and 2). Group membership opens the data plane (Wall 3). A person needs both to reach data.
- Orion is open to nobody: no persona holds Wall.Orion and no group has a role on wall-orion. Ian has no app role, so the gateway refuses every tool call he makes.
- Each server has its own managed identity and no Entra client secret. Four have a federated credential for OBO; the legacy identity is broad on purpose.
